https://www.cei.int/ansa/178469.text: Vilnius will summon Russian representative on damage sustained at the embassy in Kyiv (ANSA) - TRIESTE, AUG 2 - The Lithuanian Foreign Ministry will summon the Russian representative in Vilnius after the Lithuanian embassy building in Kyiv was damaged in a massive Russian attack. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budris reported on X that "missiles struck just meters from the Embassy" and that "fortunately, our staff did not suffer." "Russia's campaign of terror against Ukraine continues without limits. There is no sign of any genuine willingness to stop it, to seek peace or engage in negotiations" he stated, adding "The Kremlin's objective remains the same: destruction, death and intimidation. The response is clear: increase pressure on Russia through stronger sanctions and step up support for Ukraine." (ANSA). Know-how Exchange Programme Call for Proposals 2026 now open! https://wsbt.com/news/local/warsaw-hosts.text: Zimmer Biomet Center Lake Pavilion in Warsaw hosted its 9th HireKosciusko Hiring Fair on Thursday. The event allowed for those looking for jobs to meet up directly with employers face to face. 14 different companies were represented at the hiring fair, as well as higher education opportunities such as Grace College, Ivy Tech, and WorkOne Northern Indiana. Allyn Decker from OrhoWorx believes that this event helps people get through the job searching process better. "For anybody who's been in a job search recently, it can be discouraging when everything is requiring online applications," said Decker. Decker also spoke about how not going through an online application process can keep a candidate from getting automatically eliminated due to AI screening. Around 120 job seekers were expected to come to the event.

https://www.politico.eu/article/starlink.text: KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service. “Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity. “As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted,” a defense ministry official told reporters on Friday. Advertisement Advertisement Ukrainian drone units started testing speed limits from Thursday evening, shortly after Trump told reporters that Musk had restored Starlink. While some tests recorded speeds of up to 200 km/h over the Black Sea and noted an improvement, the drones still rapidly lost signal once flying above the 160 km/h speed limit. “So, the key point is: We accelerate above 180 km/h, fly for a couple of minutes, the connection drops. It falls to 140–150 km/h and then is re-established — but the situation is better,” a drone pilot from Ukraine’s top drone unit known as Magyar’s Birds told POLITICO. “So it works better, but with constant connection interruptions,” the pilot, whose call sign is Leon, said. The speed limit on Starshield, Starlink’s service designed for military purposes, stalled key operations and partially disabled crucial drone interceptors against Russian Shaheds attack drones. Musk said that the U.S. government controlled Starshield, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the administration could not direct SpaceX or Musk regarding restrictions or slowdowns of Starlink services in Ukraine as it is a private company. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy argued the Starlink restriction was a planned operation to specifically restrict Starshield’s operating speed over Ukraine. The Ukrainian government said that it was not told why that had happened for days. However, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Trump had called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions. “I don’t want to say. That’s a very interesting situation. My relationship with Elon is very good. I don’t want to comment on it, whether I called, or someone else called … The bottom line: he put it back,” Trump told reporters on Thursday evening. https://www.eldoradonews.com/news/2026/n.text: G20 envoys end summit without consensus ATLANTA -- Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies wrapped up two days of talks Saturday without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues after divisions, notably over Russia's war with Ukraine, visibly overshadowed the start of the Atlanta meeting and impacted its outcome. As a result, the group did not release a joint communique but relied on a chairman's statement summarizing the talks that Secretary of State Marco Rubio released after the meetings closed. That statement made no mention of any agreements reached. Rather, it referred to a list of priorities, from energy and food security to freedom of navigation, that G20 members determined were important to solve. "I wouldn't pretend to you today that we are close to finding universally accepted solutions to these problems," Rubio told reporters at a news conference marking the end of the meetings. "But," he said, "I do think that among the G20 represented here are countries that are working together to solve some of them, particularly in the realm of supply chains and critical minerals." Rubio had said the first day of the session was "very productive." On Saturday, he hosted sideline talks with his counterparts from Australia, India and Japan before leading the final G20 event that focused on freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red, Black and South China seas. "I made clear to our partners that secure supply chains are essential for growth," Rubio said in a social media post on X. "Critical trade routes including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb Strait must remain secure and open to commerce. And we must continue to strengthen and expand critical mineral supply chains to protect our future." At a reception for G20 participants Friday night, Rubio sounded optimistic. "Together, I think that we are mapping a vibrant, dynamic, and bold economic future, one that will pioneer new horizons for the entire world," he said. Rubio had opened the talks Friday with an appeal for unity, but then canceled the traditional group photo of the foreign ministers. European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the snapshot. Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus. "We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it's very difficult to agree on a common line," he said. Other participants in the meetings, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the private talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds and to work to make next month's summit of G20 leaders hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida a success. These diplomats said a chairman's statement had long been the plan because of the deep differences among the attendees, including over the Russia-Ukraine war, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese moves in the South China Sea. They described the opening session as cordial but said Russia's position on Ukraine was unyielding, as was its opposition to Poland's membership in the G20. They said the disagreements also included the Trump administration's decision not to invite G20 member South Africa over the objections of others. Rubio defended the decision to invite Lavrov to Atlanta and Putin to the summit, saying it would be impossible to peacefully resolve the crisis without speaking to both sides. "I don't know if negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine," he said Saturday. "That's what we're trying to find out, but I don't think anyone here is claiming that we're on the verge of a negotiated settlement." You're one step away from the full story.
